Definition: of uncertain affinity; a festival:--feast, holyday.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says heortḗ, it means feast, holyday. The word appears 23 times, and in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that heortḗ matters because God gave His people feasts so they would remember what He had done. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
RelatedEvents: The Last Supper; The Boy Jesus in the Temple
